design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (sender_verification_and_limits, category account) — kept up to date from Step 0; every assertion below names the world it is true on.

[Step 0 — draw, printed by skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0030_money_transfer_service/tasks/sender_verification_and_limits --tasks 2]
{"task": 0, "key": "env_0030_money_transfer_service/sender_verification_and_limits/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 6]}
{"task": 1, "key": "env_0030_money_transfer_service/sender_verification_and_limits/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 4]}
Task 0 therefore has exactly 1 prerequisite problem (2 problems) and two computations of 6 factors each: account_ext_limits_callback_window takes 6, account_ext_review_decision_window takes 6.

[Step 0 — asset ledger and claim]
Already occupied before this task: nothing (task 0 is the first). Claimable account writes: account_unlocked, account_level_upgraded, account_limit_review_requested, account_document_received, account_callback_scheduled, account_statement_requested, account_closed_by_customer, account_appeal_lodged. In db_schema.json the only fields of those writes a computation can land in are dates: sender_accounts.next_review_due_date (upgrade), sender_account_events.decision_due_date (limit review request), callback_due_date (callback), statement_period_start/end and delivery_due_date (statement); unlock, document logging, closure and appeal carry no number or computed date (lock_reason/locked_at, doc fields copied from the upload, closed_date = today, event_date/channel). So the difficulty's five problems are: upgrade (refresh interval months), limit review request (decision window business days, owner=user: the account holder's own request and attestation to compliance), limits callback (callback window), statement request (delivery window, owner=user: the account holder's own instruction to release their transfer history), fees callback (callback window). The two customer-owned writes are the limit review request and the statement request because closure and appeal — the other customer-owned events — carry no field a computation can land in; the blueprint summary lists the agent as lodging reviews and requesting statements, but the base event meanings ("The customer asks compliance to review the account", "The customer requests an account statement") make both the customer's own request, and every task must carry a customer write.
Claimed by task 0: account_ext_limits_callback_window (root, schedule_limits_callback_7588c2a7, owner agent) and account_ext_review_decision_window (prerequisite, lodge_limit_review_54a88584, owner user).
Left for task 1 (draw: 2 prerequisite problems, factors 5/4/4): account_ext_fees_callback_window (root) <- account_ext_statement_delivery_window (customer's own statement request) <- account_ext_upgrade_refresh_interval (agent upgrade whose level carries the statement history allowance). That tree shares no policy, tool or main dependency chain with task 0; its upgrade policy is not a prerequisite of the limit review policy (the task 0 customer already holds the level directly below the one she asks for), so the two trees stay disjoint.

[Step 0 — design thesis]
Surface goal (customer): Graciela Ibarra Montes wants a call back from Paloma's limits people about raising her sending limit — she is buying a house in Zapopan and must send about eleven thousand dollars in one go, while her per-transfer limit is 6,000.00 (Paloma Verified Plus).
Prerequisite the policy imposes (not mentioned by her): account_ext_limits_callback_window's rule states "A callback on limits and levels is not booked until the account history carries a limit review request that compliance has not yet decided." At frozen_time 2026-09-15 her only limit review request (2026-05-04, Paloma Enhanced) has a declined decision (2026-05-07), so no undecided request stands; the agent must have her lodge one herself (owner=user tool), for Paloma Enhanced, the level directly above Verified Plus.
Core computations: (1) the decision window of that request in Paloma business days (6 factors, cross-difficulty Bank/Cash/Wallet history); (2) the limits callback window in Paloma business days (6 factors), whose distance-to-decision factor reads the decision due date the request just landed (value_input edge).
Depth: surface goal -> limits callback rule -> prerequisite sentence -> history shows the May request already decided -> customer's own review request (decision window computed) -> callback window computed on the world that now carries the undecided request. Breadth: tier params (Verified Plus review-time table, callback_sla_business_days, per_transfer_limit_usd, dedicated_support_line), 24/12/6/1-month windows over the account history, Bank Deposit ledger and cases, Cash Pickup ledger, Mobile Wallet ledger.
[Why this is a good test] The customer asks for one thing — a call back from the limits people. Nothing she says names a review, a level or a document. The agent must (1) find in the limits callback rule that the callback waits on an undecided limit review request, (2) read the account history and see the only request (2026-05-04) already carries a declined decision, (3) work out from the limit review policy that the request is the customer's own write and that the level requested must be the one directly above Verified Plus (Paloma Enhanced), (4) compute a six-factor decision window from four products' records, hand the tool over and let her lodge it, and (5) compute a six-factor callback window on the world that now carries her request. Difficulty comes from reading policy, querying eight record types and arithmetic, never from choosing between look-alike tools: there is exactly one review-request tool and one limits-callback tool.

[Base-invariant card]
Write 1 — account_limit_review_requested (step 14). Governing base policies: account_sending_limits (no structured gate; the write books no transfer and raises no limit) and account_evt_limit_review with six gates, all true on the opening world:
 account_active — "A limit review request is accepted only while the account status is active." sender_accounts.status = active.
 next_review_level — "The requested level must be exactly one level above the current level (level_number one higher), and that level's review_required_for_entry must be true" — variant Paloma Verified Plus (level 3) -> Paloma Enhanced (level 4, review_required_for_entry true).
 documents_logged — Enhanced requires government_id, selfie, ssn_itin, proof_of_address, occupation_employer (latest reviews accepted 2024-02-13 / 2026-04-17) and source_of_funds: the latest source-of-funds document UPL-19306128 (received 2026-09-10, submitted_for_level Paloma Enhanced) has no review row, so it is pending_review for the requested level; the earlier UPL-18154407 was rejected too_old and is superseded.
 decline_cooldown (time) — anchor event "the most recent declined limit review decision", anchor_source sender_account_events.event_date = 2026-05-07, duration variants.limit_review_cooldown_days of the level that decision concerned (Paloma Enhanced: 60), calendar days, relation not_before, inclusive: earliest new request 2026-07-06; 2026-07-05 would fail, 2026-07-06 passes; 2026-09-15 passes.
 no_undecided_request — the only request (cd561081...) has a decision row pointing back to it.
 review_frequency — Verified Plus limit_review_max_per_180d = 2; requests dated on 2026-03-20 or later (the 180-day window ending 2026-09-15) = 1 (2026-05-04), plus the new one = 2 <= 2.
Write 2 — account_callback_scheduled (step 16). Governing base policy account_evt_service_entitlements, gate callback_account_open ("A callback can be scheduled for any account that is not closed.") — status active. Its due-date sentence is superseded for limits callbacks by account_ext_limits_callback_window's declared overwrite; for every other topic the base sentence still governs.

[Business-object card] Object of write 1: the customer's single Personal Sender Account (53bcfa0c...), keyed by sender_account_id; the request is a new history entry, no existing row is touched. Object of write 2: the same account; the callback is a new history entry on topic limits_and_levels. Aggregates: account-history rows are those of this sender_account_id; Bank/Cash/Wallet ledger rows are those whose transfer belongs to this customer (all transfers carry customer_id and this sender_account_id). Excluded by the rules' own words: the 2026-03-15 Bank Deposit information answer (exactly 6 months back), the 2025-09-15 recipient addition (exactly 12 months back), the Bank Deposit funds-received and fee entries (only payouts sent count), the 2,999.00 payout (not the Verified Plus ceiling), Cash Pickup funds-received and fee entries. No reversal, refund or adjustment exists on any transfer.

[Factor card — account_ext_review_decision_window, handling-time world = opening world (step 14 is the first write)]
 baseline (computation document): standard decision window = review time of the level requested = 3 (Paloma Enhanced). All factors at fall-through -> 3.
 level_seasoning (parameter; ladder <30 days +2 / 30-179 +1 / otherwise 0): level_effective_date 2026-04-20, 148 days -> +1; baseline gives 12.
 earlier_declines (parameter, multi-source; declined AND request for information +2 / declined AND no request for information +1 / otherwise 0): decision 2026-05-07 declined, request for information 2025-10-06 -> +2; baseline 11.
 recent_sending (parameter, cross-difficulty bank+cash+wallet; >=20,000.00 +2 / 8,000.00-19,999.99 +1 / otherwise 0): 18,569.00 -> +1; baseline 12.
 fresh_documents (parameter; >=3 +2 / 1-2 +1 / otherwise 0): 1 (UPL-19306128) -> +1; baseline 12.
 cash_reliance (parameter, cross-difficulty cash; >=8 +2 / 4-7 +1 / otherwise 0): 5 payouts -> +1; baseline 12.
 review_escalation (method; >=4 recipients: round up to a multiple of 5 / 2-3: plus half rounded up / otherwise as counted): 3 -> 9 + 5 = 14; baseline 9.
 Near-miss: recipient Wendy Ibarra Coyoy added 2025-09-15 — counting it gives 4 recipients and the weekly committee (9 -> 10). Stamp: none; every tier rests on dated rows.
[Factor card — account_ext_limits_callback_window, handling-time world = opening world + step 14]
 baseline: callback_sla_business_days of Paloma Verified Plus = 2. All factors at fall-through -> 2.
 decision_distance (parameter, value_input from step 14; >=14 days +2 / 7-13 +1 / otherwise 0): decision due 2026-10-05, 20 days -> +2; baseline 5.
 account_age (parameter; <12 months +2 / 12-35 +1 / otherwise 0): opened 2024-02-12, 31 months -> +1; baseline 6.
 answered_transfer_information (parameter, cross-difficulty bank; >=2 +2 / exactly 1 +1 / none 0): 1 (2026-04-29) -> +1; baseline 6. Near-miss: the 2026-03-15 answer (exactly 6 months back) would make 2 -> +2.
 new_payees (parameter; >=4 +2 / 2-3 +1 / otherwise 0): 3 -> +1; baseline 6.
 ceiling_payouts (parameter, cross-difficulty bank; >=3 take off 3 / 1-2 take off 2 / none 0): 2 payouts of 6,000.00 -> -2; baseline 11. Near-miss: the 2,999.00 payout of 2026-04-03 equals the ceiling of the level held then (Verified), not of the level held now.
 callback_queue (method; earlier callback still due: plus half rounded up / none due and dedicated line: half rounded up / otherwise as counted): the 2026-09-11 documents callback is due 2026-09-15 -> 5 + 3 = 8; baseline 5.
 Inherited base boundaries: both policies keep every base eligibility gate (listed above); account_ext_review_decision_window only supersedes the decision-due-date sentence of account_evt_limit_review, account_ext_limits_callback_window supersedes two sentences of account_evt_service_entitlements for the limits topic, both declared in its overwrite: the callback-due-date sentence, and "A level with dedicated_support_line true is called back from the priority line, and a level with relationship_manager_assigned true is called back by the named relationship manager; neither changes the due date." (its queue step lets the priority line halve the window of a limits callback when no earlier callback is still due; on this world the account is Verified Plus, without a dedicated line, so that tier does not apply). Apart from these declared replacements no new product law is made: the review times are the base limit_review_sla_business_days, the callback SLA, per-transfer limit and dedicated-line flag are base tier parameters; the factors refine how long compliance and the limits desk take for a given file.

[Problem-tree card]
 Root: account_ext_limits_callback_window (schedule_limits_callback_7588c2a7, owner agent; 6 factors). Prerequisite: account_ext_review_decision_window (lodge_limit_review_54a88584, owner user; 6 factors).
 Edge: kind value_input, gate decision_gap_days, form state; prerequisite sentence (the blocked policy's own rule, negated direction, the way a booking desk states what a booking waits for): "A callback on limits and levels is not booked until the account history carries a limit review request that compliance has not yet decided." Four-point test: (1) ordering connective "not ... until" joins this policy's result (the callback being booked) to the state; the affirmative rewrite "is booked only after the account history carries ..." adds or drops nothing; (2) the waited-on side is a record-visible state (an undecided limit review request on the account history); (3) no tool, id or code token; (4) hard requirement ("not ... until"), scope exactly the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: the limit review request (account_ext_review_decision_window's write); the upgrade, statement and callback writes never create a limit review request. Derivation: sentence + history (the May request is decided) + the limit review policy's rule (its write is the request, dated the request date, carrying the decision due date) -> lodge a new request. Why false at the opening: initial_state.sender_account_events.f2083685... related_event_id points to the only request and review_outcome = declined. Deletion sensitivity (sens run): without step 14 the callback window is 5, not 8, and the request row is missing.
 Topological order: account_ext_review_decision_window (step 14) -> account_ext_limits_callback_window (step 16). Single edge, so no parallel-order question.
 user_scenario never names the review, a level, documents or compliance; tools validate nothing (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block).

[Persona design] Voice: a hurried, warm dental assistant on her lunch break; she volunteers only the goal (a call back about raising her limit for the Zapopan house), the mobile number, and the authorisation to book the call back today. Given only when asked: date of birth, ZIP, ID last four, email, why she needs more, her recent upload, the May refusal, the pending documents call. Passive reactions: agrees to do "something on the account herself" when the agent explains it; runs the handed-over tool with exactly the level and number the agent gives; goes with whatever level the agent names (no level is named by her); ends once the callback is confirmed with its date. No ask of her own beyond the callback; the last reaction answers the last gold action (the booked callback).

[Reachability walk] Turn 1 goal + phone -> find_customers; verification credentials on request -> verify_customer_identity; account, history, documents, recipients and the three products' transfers/ledgers/cases are all readable by the share tools with her customer or account reference; the KB for the limits callback states the prerequisite sentence; the limit review policy states that the request is the customer's own ask and how its window is worked out; the agent hands the tool over (unlock_user_discoverable_tool), she runs it and reads back decision due date 2026-10-05 (the return enters the transcript); the agent unlocks and books the callback, tells her the due date 2026-09-25, and she closes. Everything happens at frozen_time 2026-09-15 11:20 CDT; no step waits for a review decision, a document review or a call.

[Places most easily got wrong] counting the 2025-09-15 recipient (escalation and new payees both shift a tier); counting the 2026-03-15 information answer; treating the 2,999.00 payout as a ceiling payout; summing booked principal or funds-received entries instead of payouts; reading the decision window from the requested level's base SLA alone (3) or the callback window from the base SLA alone (2); computing the callback distance on the opening world (the May request, -131 days) instead of after her request; booking the callback without the request; lodging the request for Paloma Premier; having the agent call the customer-owned tool.

[Standard solution] Locate by phone, verify with phone + date of birth + ZIP; read account, history, documents, recipients, Bank/Cash/Wallet transfers, ledgers and Bank cases; hand over lodge_limit_review_54a88584 and have her lodge {sender_account_id, requested_level: Paloma Enhanced, decision_window_business_days: 14}; unlock schedule_limits_callback_7588c2a7 and book {sender_account_id, callback_window_business_days: 8}.

user_scenario:
You are Graciela Ibarra Montes, forty-five, a dental assistant in southwest Houston, calling Paloma Remit on your lunch break from the clinic parking lot. You are warm and polite but a bit hurried, you speak English with the odd Spanish word slipping in, and you keep your answers short because you only have a few minutes. Your family is buying a small house in Zapopan, Jalisco, and the notary there needs roughly eleven thousand dollars for the down payment and the deed costs by the end of the month; when you tried to send it last week the app stopped you at six thousand per transfer. What you want from this call is one thing: you want somebody from Paloma's sending-limits people to call you back about raising your limit so the house money can go in one go. You are happy for the agent to book that call back for you today; you are not trying to send any money on this call.

You open by saying you need a call back from whoever handles sending limits, and you give your mobile number, 7135550104, straight away so they can find you. When the agent asks to verify you, you give your date of birth, 1981-07-23, and your ZIP code, 77036; if they want one more thing you give the last four of your photo ID, 1Q74, and if they ask for your email it is gibarra.montes@outlook.com. You do not know what level your account is at, what Paloma calls its levels, or how its reviews work, and you do not guess.

Only when the agent asks why you need more, you explain it is the house in Zapopan, paid from your own savings at your credit union. Only when the agent asks whether you have uploaded anything lately, you say you sent a letter from the credit union about your savings last week through the app. Only when the agent asks whether you ever asked for higher limits before, you say yes, back in May, and that they turned you down because a paper you sent was too old. Only when the agent asks whether somebody else is already supposed to call you, you say someone from the documents side was meant to call you about your papers, but nobody has called yet.

If the agent explains that something has to be done on your account before the limits people can call you and that it is something you have to do yourself, you agree right away and say you will do it on your phone while you are on the line. When the agent sends it to you, you go through it with exactly the level and the number of business days the agent gives you, and you read back the reference number and the date it shows you. If the agent asks you which level you want, you say you do not know the names, you just need whatever comes next that lets you send about eleven thousand at once; if the agent tells you which level it should be, you go with the level the agent names.

Once the agent tells you the call back is booked and by when they will call, you say thank you, that works, and you hang up.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A new request may be lodged only once limit_review_cooldown_days calendar days have passed since the most recent declined limit review decision.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The cooldown is counted in calendar days from the event_date of that declined decision, using the cooldown of the level that decision concerned, so the earliest new request date is that event_date plus the cooldown days.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's customer profile from the mobile number she states at the opening, returning her customer reference number and the profile attributes used to verify her.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and both writes are keyed on her customer and account reference numbers; without the profile no account can be found.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record the in-session identity verification with three stated credentials (mobile number, date of birth, ZIP code) matched against the profile.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Paloma requires the caller's identity to be verified before discussing or changing anything on her account; three matches is the verification threshold.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her Personal Sender Account: level Paloma Verified Plus, status active, opened_date 2024-02-12, level_effective_date 2026-04-20.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The level fixes the level requested (the one directly above Verified Plus is Paloma Enhanced, review time review_days_enhanced), the standard limits callback window (callback_sla_business_days of Verified Plus), the per-transfer ceiling (6,000.00) and the dedicated-line test; the opening and level dates feed the account-age and time-at-level factors; status active satisfies both writes' state gates.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the account history: the 2026-05-04 limit review request for Paloma Enhanced and its 2026-05-07 declined decision, the 2025-10-06 request for information, six recipient additions (three of them after 2025-09-15) and the 2026-09-11 documents callback due 2026-09-15.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: This is the read that shows the limits callback's prerequisite is unmet ("A callback on limits and levels is not booked until the account history carries a limit review request that compliance has not yet decided." — the only request is already decided), and it carries the evidence of the earlier-declines, escalation, new-payees and callback-queue factors, plus the cooldown, frequency and no-undecided-request gates of the review request.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.sender_account_id: Value: the customer's Personal Sender Account reference number returned by find_sender_accounts (step 2). Basis: the lodge tool docstring — "the Personal Sender Account reference number of the account the review is for, as returned by the Personal Sender Account lookup for this customer"; the seed holds one sender account for this customer (initial_state.sender_accounts). Uniqueness: a customer holds at most one Personal Sender Account (account_agg_multi_holding: "Each customer may hold at most one Personal Sender Account"), so no other reference number is reachable.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.requested_level: Value: Paloma Enhanced. Basis: account_evt_limit_review — "The requested level must be exactly one level above the current level (level_number one higher), and that level's review_required_for_entry must be true"; find_sender_accounts shows variant_name Paloma Verified Plus (level_number 3), so the next level is Paloma Enhanced (level 4), whose review_required_for_entry is true. Uniqueness: Paloma Premier and Paloma Private Client are two and three levels up and are excluded by "exactly one level above"; Paloma Starter, Paloma Verified and Paloma Verified Plus are at or below the level held; none names no level (the docstring: "the marker the account history carries on entries that are not limit review requests"). The customer only says she needs "whatever comes next" and goes with the level the agent names; the persona never names it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.decision_window_business_days: Value: 14. Standard decision window: the level requested is Paloma Enhanced -> review_days_enhanced = 3. Time at the current level: level_effective_date 2026-04-20 is 148 calendar days before 2026-09-15 (30 <= 148 < 180) -> +1. Earlier declined decisions: the 2026-05-07 declined decision and the 2025-10-06 request for information both fall in the 24 months -> +2. Recent sending: Bank Deposit payouts after 2026-03-15 total 17,699.00, Cash Pickup 750.00, Mobile Wallet 120.00 -> 18,569.00 (8,000.00 <= x < 20,000.00) -> +1. Fresh documents: one document (UPL-19306128, received 2026-09-10) after 2026-08-15 -> +1. Cash reliance: five Cash Pickup payouts after 2025-09-15 (4 <= 5 < 8) -> +1. Counted decision window 3+1+2+1+1+1 = 9. Escalation: three recipients added after 2025-09-15 (2 <= 3 < 4; the 2025-09-15 addition no longer counts) -> second reviewer: 9 plus half of 9 rounded up (5) = 14. Any agent applying the rule on this world converges on 14; the fixed-format contract is a whole number of Paloma business days, and the tool lands decision due date 2026-10-05.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect; once per task.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Book the callback on limits and levels the customer asked for, due the computed number of Paloma business days from 2026-09-15.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: account_ext_limits_callback_window computes callback_window_business_days on the world that now carries the undecided review request.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.sender_account_id: Value: the same Personal Sender Account reference number returned by find_sender_accounts (step 2). Basis: the callback tool docstring — "the Personal Sender Account reference number of the customer to be called back, as returned by the Personal Sender Account lookup for this customer". Uniqueness: one account per customer; it is also the account the step-14 request was lodged on.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.callback_window_business_days: Value: 8. Standard limits callback window: callback_sla_business_days of Paloma Verified Plus = 2. Distance to the review decision: the step-14 receipt shows decision_due_date 2026-10-05, 20 calendar days after 2026-09-15 (>= 14) -> +2. Account age: opened 2024-02-12, 31 whole months (12 <= 31 < 36) -> +1. Transfer information already answered: one Bank Deposit information answer after 2026-03-15 (2026-04-29; the 2026-03-15 answer is exactly 6 months back) -> +1. New payees: three recipients added after 2025-09-15 (2 <= 3 < 4) -> +1. Payouts at the per-transfer ceiling: two Bank Deposit payouts of exactly 6,000.00 (the Verified Plus per_transfer_limit_usd) after 2026-03-15 (1 <= 2 < 3) -> 2 taken off. Counted limits callback window 2+2+1+1+1-2 = 5. Queue step: the 2026-09-11 documents callback is due 2026-09-15, on the request date, so the new callback waits behind it: 5 plus half of 5 rounded up (3) = 8; never fewer than 1. The tool lands callback due date 2026-09-25.

edges.condition: sender_account_events holds, for this sender account, a row of event_type account_limit_review_requested with no account_limit_review_decided row pointing back to it.
edges.policy_source: A callback on limits and levels is not booked until the account history carries a limit review request that compliance has not yet decided.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-09-15 the account history carries exactly one limit review request (2026-05-04, Paloma Enhanced) and a decision row points back to it with outcome declined, so no undecided request stands; the most recent request's decision due date, 2026-05-07, lies 131 days before the handling date.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The customer's own limit review request (step 14) lands a new account_limit_review_requested row dated 2026-09-15, requested_level Paloma Enhanced, decision_due_date 2026-10-05, with no decision pointing to it; decision_gap_days becomes 20 and the distance addition becomes far_decision_add (2).

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: One edge, no parallel prerequisites: the limits callback's own rule pins the order ("A callback on limits and levels is not booked until the account history carries a limit review request that compliance has not yet decided."), and the callback's distance-to-decision factor reads the decision due date the request writes, so the request (step 14) strictly precedes the callback (step 16). The review request's own computation reads no callback field (its factors read level dates, declines, requests for information, payouts, documents and recipients), so the callback written later cannot change it.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 14 (sens run, _scratch/sens.py 0): the request row is missing from the terminal state, pending_decision_due falls back to the declined May request (2026-05-07), decision_gap_days = -131 instead of 20, decision_distance_days 0 instead of 2, counted window 3 instead of 5 and callback_window_business_days 5 instead of 8 (callback due 2026-09-22 instead of 2026-09-25).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for a call back from the sending-limits people; it never mentions a limit review, a review request, documents to submit, levels or compliance. Her earlier refusal in May, her recent upload and the pending documents callback are each said only when the agent asks about them, and her cooperation ("If the agent explains that something has to be done on your account before the limits people can call you and that it is something you have to do yourself, you agree right away") is a passive reaction to the agent's explanation.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py: schedule_limits_callback_7588c2a7 reads only the sender account (to copy customer_id) and creates the callback row whatever the account history holds — it never looks for a limit review request, never refuses and never hints; lodge_limit_review_54a88584 likewise creates the request without checking level, documents, cooldown or frequency. Calling the callback tool with no undecided request still writes a callback, only with a different window, which the terminal hash catches.
